correctness.rationale: For all even k>=2 and odd p, the geometric sum with base p^k congruent 1 modulo 8 has exact 2-adic valuation nu_2(b+1); multiplicativity yields both necessary and sufficient cross-divisibility conditions. The bound a<2k follows from b>=2^a-1, p^b<=S_{k,a}, and 2^a-1>=k(a+1) for a>=2k. A separate induction at k=2 excludes a>=3, exact 27>21 excludes a=2, and S_{2,1}=5 gives n=10, checked directly by sigma_2(10)=130. The Python standard-library certificate enumerates k=2,4 within rigorous bounds and checks 2268 valuation instances; it is not substituted for the infinite argument.

value.rationale: General divisibility n|sigma_k(n) was shown to have infinitely many even solutions for fixed k>=2, but the natural restriction to one odd prime support was not known to force finiteness. The theorem establishes a uniform exponent cutoff and exact effective classification across all even k, and completely resolves the first parameter k=2. This structural contrast motivates the precise restriction and invariant; it is not a finite table extrapolation or an arbitrary slice.
